title: Check yourself: A claims assistant end to end, across the seven domains

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Scenario: Larch Mutual's assistant answers a coverage question with a limit of 3,000, and the current policy says 5,000. Latency and the model version have not changed since the documents were refreshed. Where does the investigation start?

options.text: The retrieval step, to see whether a stale chunk was returned
options.says: A confident wrong answer after a refresh points to stale evidence.

options.text: The model, to see whether its weights were updated by the vendor
options.says: Ruled out because the stem leaves the model version unchanged, and the page says "check the version of the evidence before the model".

options.text: The sampling temperature, to see whether it was lowered by a release
options.says: Ruled out because "Fix the wrong answer in the prompt; the model got it wrong" is the tempting lever the exam rejects, and a temperature change would not return the exact old figure.

options.text: The context window, to see whether the prompt was cut short
options.says: Ruled out because the stale index holds the chunk "Water damage is covered up to 3,000 per claim.", the very figure the assistant gave, which a cut-short prompt would not produce.

questions.stem: Scenario: A change to the retrieval step gains three answers in a minor segment and loses one in the segment where an error costs 250. The totals favour the change. What does the gate return?

options.text: Release it, because the gains outnumber the losses
options.says: Ruled out because "a loss in a protected segment is a veto whatever the gains elsewhere".

options.text: Release it, with a note asking the owner to review the lost case
options.says: Ruled out because the gate returns a decision and not a note, and the page says it "says no-go and names the segment".

options.text: Refuse it, naming the area where the damage fell
options.says: A loss in a protected segment is a veto whatever the gains.

options.text: Refuse it, because every loss blocks every change
options.says: Ruled out because the gate's rule is that "the losses do not outnumber the gains" for a loss outside a protected segment, so not every loss blocks a change.

concepts: Traps, as the page teaches it
